body.p: Claims 1-15 are pending in the application. Claims 1, 2, 3, 6, 12, 14 and 15 are amended. No new matter is added. Applicant's amendments and remarks should not be construed as forfeiting any subject matter described in the specification. Applicant's amendments are made solely for the purposes of advancing prosecution in this application. Applicant reserves the right to pursue the original and previously presented claims and any and all other claims in this and other related applications.
Claims 3, 6, 7, 13 and 14 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §112 as being indefinite for
failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter. Claims 3, 6, and 12 (from which claim 13 depends) and 14 have been amended to obviate the rejection.
Claims 1-8, 10, 11, 14, and 15 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Krieger (US 5,830,183). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.

Embodiments of claim 1 concern a retaining clip (or holding device) for long flexible elements allowing for quick and easy rolling up into a spiral coil and secure holding. As such, claim 1 is amended to recite, inter alia, a gripper having a tube-shaped center part and a latch extending away from and fixedly attached to the tube-shaped center, the latch having a radial distance around at least a part of the circumference of the tube-shaped center part and defining a curved receiving space that is configured to remain open.
As best understood by Applicant, Krieger fails to disclose, teach, or suggest the
limitations of claim 1. For example, Krieger fails to disclose, teach, or suggest a latch extending

away from and "fixedly attached" to the tube-shaped center. In addition, Krieger fails to disclose, teach, or suggest the latch having a radial distance around at least a part of the circumference of the tube-shaped center part and defining a curved receiving space that is "configured to remain open."
Claim 1 is therefore allowable over the cited art. Claims 2-8, 10, 11, and 14 depend from claim 1 and are allowable for at least the same reasons and on their own merit.
Claim 15 is also allowable over Krieger because Krieger fails to disclose, teach or

suggest "a tube-shaped center part from which a latch extends away in radial distance to the center part around at least a part of the circumference of the center part to define a holding space that extends more than a half turn around a center axis of the center part."
Claims 1-9, 11, 14, and 15 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Poulsen (US 5,309,604). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
As best understood by Applicant, Poulsen fails to disclose, teach, or suggest the

limitations of claim 1. For example, Poulsen fails to disclose, teach, or suggest a latch having a radial distance around at least a part of the circumference of the tube-shaped center part and defining a curved receiving space that is "configured to remain open."
Claim 1 is therefore allowable over the cited art. Claims 2-9, 11, and 14 depend from claim 1 and are allowable for at least the same reasons and on their own merit.
Claim 15 is also allowable over Poulsen because Poulsen fails to disclose, teach or

suggest "a tube-shaped center part from which a latch extends away in radial distance to the center part around at least a part of the circumference of the center part to define a holding space that extends more than a half turn around a center axis of the center part."

Claims 12 and 13 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Poulsen (US 5,309,604), in view of Alden (US 5,364,355). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection as Alden fails to cure the deficiencies of Poulsen (discussed above with respect to claim 1).

Applicant submits the rejections be withdrawn. Applicants believe the application is now in condition for allowance and respectfully requests a notice to that effect. Should the Examiner believe that any additional minor amendment to the claims be made to place the application in even better condition for allowance, the Examiner is cordially invited to telephone the attorney of record identified below.
The undersigned representative requests any extension of time that may be deemed

necessary to further the prosecution of this application. The undersigned representative authorizes the Commissioner to charge any additional fees under 37 C.F.R. 1.16 or 1.17 that may be required, or credit any overpayment, to Deposit Account No.: 23-2185 under Order No. 200380-00286.
